The third emperor of the Qing dynasty of China, who reigned from 1661 to 1722. His 61 years on the throne are the longest of any Chinese emperor, and he made Manchu rule over China secure.

He came to the throne at seven and took power from his regent while still a teenager. Then he won a series of hard wars:

  • He crushed the Revolt of the Three Feudatories, Chinese generals in the south, in 1681.
  • He took Taiwan from the heirs of Koxinga in 1683.
  • He agreed the Treaty of Nerchinsk with Russia in 1689, fixing the northern border.
  • He fought the Dzungar Mongols in person in the 1690s.

He won over Chinese scholars by backing learning on a huge scale. Projects under his name include the Kangxi Dictionary of 1716 and a vast collection of Tang poetry. He studied mathematics and astronomy with Jesuits at his court and, for a time, allowed Christian missions. His long reign began the prosperous era that his grandson Qianlong carried on, and China's population grew fast.
